inconsistencies: #36330 and #34533 solve the same problem (periodic wallet rebroadcast leaking node IP when -privatebroadcast is set) with mutually exclusive approaches: suppress resubmission entirely vs. route it through private broadcast. Review #36330 first as the decision point; they should not both merge.
#35558 is stacked on #35724 (the reconstruction-logging split); #35724 must be reviewed and merged first even though it is only logging, which is why it was raised out of P4.

Private broadcast cluster all builds on merged #29415: #36277 and #34322 (behaviour/persistence), #34707 (observability, concept NACK from instagibbs), #34271 (cleanup), #36319 (doc backport). The scope question raised on #34707 should be settled before it is reviewed on its own terms.
#34213 and #34486 both concern node behaviour while networkactive=0 and touch overlapping CConnman state; coordinate so anchor caching and the port-mapping/Tor lifecycle changes do not conflict.

#36015 and #35919 both touch TxOrphanage limits and eviction; #36015 changes the storage representation while #35919 fixes the trimming assertion. Review together and land the crash fix in a form compatible with the serialized-storage change.

Refactor chain in net_processing/net will conflict with each other: #30988 (CConnman split), #35040 (local address manager), #34824 (TxRelay), #35561 (CNodeState fields), #34565 (BlockDownloadManager), #35502 and #35522 (move-only function splits). A merge order should be agreed before reviewing any of them in depth; the move-only splits are cheapest to rebase and should follow, not precede, the structural ones.

#35591 is explicitly marked DO NOT MERGE and the author states it will be carved into smaller PRs; it is reference material for the Erlay project rather than a review target, despite the high importance of the underlying problem.
#36300 (32.x) and #36319 (31.x) are backports of already-merged master work; their importance is inherited and they need release-branch verification, not fresh design review.
result.notes: The P2 band is large (22 PRs) because this category genuinely has many attack-resistance, privacy and relay-correctness fixes of similar consequence; ordering within the band separates them. Only #36015 rises to P1: it is the one remote, unauthenticated memory-exhaustion vector where another release cycle of exposure would be seriously harmful. Security-class fixes (#36142, #35888, #35919, #36170, #36305) sit at the top of P2, then transaction-origin privacy, then relay correctness and performance, then features, matching the category's stated ordering.
